Runbooks still say "renew the SSL certificate" when the browser warning is obsolete protocol. The certificate can be brand new. The tunnel is still TLS 1.0. This is a shortened English note. The tables, handshake diagram, and OpenSSL CLI checks live on the original post: https://sunshout.tistory.com/2206 SSL is a Netscape protocol from the 1990s. SSL 3.0 is withdrawn (POODLE and friends). What every browser speaks now is TLS, currently 1.2 or 1.3. People still say "SSL cert" because vendors sold that phrase. The file is an X.509 certificate. The handshake that uses it is TLS.

entry.summary: First post in a build-in-public series about verdict, an MCP server that gives coding agents structured, sandboxed test feedback. Watch a coding agent work and you'll see it run pytest in your shell, unsandboxed, and then push 40,000 tokens of raw output through its context window to answer one question: did my change break anything?
